public_rationale: The six-month date has arrived, but the evidence does not settle the specific forecast. Investor concern about token spending is documented earlier in 2026. It is not tied to a verified population of startups spending at least 10% of personnel costs, nor to their difficulty convincing investors around October 28. The deadline passing does not turn missing evidence into a failed forecast.
limitations: Private startup budgets and investor discussions are poorly disclosed.
General fundraising success or enterprise cost controls cannot substitute for the specified investor response.
The monetary threshold has an unknown accounting basis.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In six months, startups spending 10% or more of headcount costs on AI tokens will have a hard time convincing investors that the spending is necessary.

statement.excerpt: I also think that startups burning 10% or more of their headcount in AI tokens will have a tough time convincing investors in six months that doing so is necessary.

from_speaker: 10% or more of their headcount in AI tokens
our_interpretation: Headcount means personnel costs, rather than a count of employees, because the sentence compares spending amounts.
Six calendar months after April 28 is October 28, 2026.
The surrounding discussion concerns tokens used by staff for internal work, rather than all inference costs incurred delivering a startup's product.
A tough time means substantive investor resistance, demands for justification or cuts, or financing difficulties explicitly linked to that spending.
The wording describes a general tendency among qualifying startups. An isolated anecdote cannot establish that tendency.
The spending threshold defines the target group; it is not a separate conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence around October 28, 2026 shows a broad pattern of investor resistance to internal token spending among startups documented to spend at least 10% of personnel costs on it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence for the same qualifying population and period shows investors generally accept the spending as necessary without the predicted difficulty.
